mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% within the last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annual growth rate falls below -2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% within the same month signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes purchasing power, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 202 (approx. 2% above 200 base) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates population reclassification or labor force re-entry without job creation, which signals weak labor market quality and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
regime_hint: labor force re-entry without job growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals sustained weakness in consumer demand, which reduces revenue expectations for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.
